verses.text: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.
Job said:
"Let the day I was born be wiped out, and the night that said, 'A boy is coming!'
Let that day turn into darkness. Let God above not care about it. Let no light shine on it.
Let darkness and deep shadow take it back. Let a cloud settle over it. Let blackness frighten it away.
Let thick darkness grab that night. Let it not be counted among the days of the year. Let it not be part of any month.
Let that night be empty. Let no shout of joy be heard in it.
Let those who curse days curse it, those who are ready to wake up the sea monster Leviathan.
Let its morning stars stay dark. Let it wait for light that never comes. Let it never see the first rays of dawn.
It did not close my mother's womb to keep me from being born, and it did not hide trouble from my eyes.
Why didn't I die at birth? Why didn't I die as I came from my mother's body?
Why was there a lap to hold me, and breasts to feed me?
If I had died then, I would be lying down in peace. I would be asleep and at rest,
with kings and their advisers, who built great buildings that are now ruins,
or with rulers who had gold and filled their houses with silver.
Why wasn't I buried like a baby born dead, like a baby that never saw the light?
In death the wicked stop causing trouble, and the tired find rest.
Prisoners rest together there. They no longer hear the shouts of the slave driver.
The small and the great are there, and the slave is free from his master.
Why does God give light to those who suffer, and life to those whose hearts are bitter?
They long for death, but it does not come. They search for it more than for hidden treasure.
They would be filled with joy and glad to reach the grave.
Why give light to a man who cannot see where he is going, whom God has fenced in?
My sighs are my food, and my groans pour out like water.
What I was afraid of has come on me. What I dreaded has happened to me.
I have no peace, no quiet, and no rest. Only trouble comes."
